dossier.candidate: Cleaning services (residential, move-in/move-out, short-term rental turnover, post-construction). Primary market Greater Toronto Area, with notes on Vancouver, Calgary, Ottawa and Montreal where evidence was found.
dossier.summary:
IMPORTANT, READ FIRST (how this was researched): I ran 10 WebSearch calls. Only 7 returned results; the other 3 were refused because the session-wide limit of 200 searches was already used up. The unanswered ones were Airbnb turnover rates, post-construction rates, and insurance/bonding cost. WebFetch was blocked by the network egress proxy on every domain I tried: homestars.com, hellamaid.ca, urbantasker.com, toronto.ca, www2.gov.bc.ca, canada.ca, nationalobserver.com, jobbank.gc.ca, support.taskrabbit.com and reddit.com. So every fact below comes from search-result titles and summaries, not from pages I opened. Where a summary mixed several pages, I say that I could not confirm which page a number came from. Please re-check prices before publishing them.

FINDINGS:
(1) Pricing. GTA pricing is well documented by 2026 industry blogs:
- $35–$65 per hour per cleaner; reputable companies mostly charge $45–$55.
- Registered companies charge $40–$90 per hour.
- Independent cleaners are reported at $15–$30 per hour. This shows strong low-price competition.
- TaskRabbit Toronto lists one-time cleaning from $35/hr.
- Move-out flat rates range from "from $185" at one firm to $325–$559 + HST by bedroom count at another.

(2) Platforms. TaskRabbit charges Taskers a one-time $25 registration fee, and clients pay the service fee. In Canada you must be 19 or older. Jiffy's commission is reported at 12–18% and is not fixed by contract. Some Jiffy Pro user reviews say 25–30%. Jiffy pays on the Friday after the week the job was done.

(3) Short-term rental (STR) rules reduce turnover demand in the two biggest markets:
- Toronto allows STRs only in the host's principal residence, and entire-home rentals are capped at 180 nights a year. The 2026 registration fee is $375 new / $390 renewal (from third-party guides).
- BC's principal-residence requirement took effect May 1, 2024. From May 2024 to Feb 2025, entire-home listings fell 22% in Vancouver, 24% in Victoria and 31% in Kelowna (ministry figures reported by the National Observer).

(4) Tax. The CRA small-supplier threshold is $30,000 over four consecutive calendar quarters. At the revenue needed for $5k net, the owner would have to register for GST/HST in roughly month 5, which is outside the 60-day window.

(5) Not found in this session: supply costs, liability insurance and bonding premiums, post-construction rates, Airbnb per-turnover rates, earnings reports from solo cleaners, documented failure stories (apart from the Jiffy commission complaints), and any pricing or regulation data for Calgary, Ottawa or Montreal.

VERDICT: This is one of the fastest and cheapest ways to get to first revenue, if the owner can do full-time physical work. It is a labour business: $5k net means about 26–41 billable hours a week (see the math section). The owner would have to reach that from zero reviews, against well-established insured companies and low-priced independents. Averaging $5k net over the first 60 days is unlikely. Reaching a $5k/month run rate by month 2–3 is possible for a fit, English-capable owner, ideally with a vehicle. The best-supported services are move-out/move-in and deep cleans at flat rates, plus recurring residential clients. STR turnover should be a secondary line in Toronto and Vancouver because of the rules above.
dossier.time_to_first_revenue:
ESTIMATE: 1–3 weeks from starting, if the owner is physically available.

BASIS:
- (a) TaskRabbit runs an active Toronto cleaning category, listed "from $35 an hour" for one-time cleaning (https://www.taskrabbit.ca/locations/toronto/one-time). Taskers pay a one-time $25 registration fee, and paying it does not guarantee acceptance (https://support.taskrabbit.com/hc/en-ca/articles/360032936511-What-s-the-Registration-Fee; summary only, page fetch blocked). How long approval or onboarding takes: NOT FOUND.
- (b) Jiffy pays pros on the Friday after the week the job was done (search summary for "Jiffy app cleaning pro commission fees Canada"; sources listed included https://urbantasker.com/blog/is-jiffy-on-demand-app-good-for-contractors and https://www.ratehub.ca/blog/review-jiffy-on-demand-home-service-app/). ESTIMATE: payout lags the job by 5 days (job on Sunday, paid the next Friday) to 11 days (job on Monday, paid Friday of the following week). Jiffy pro approval time: NOT FOUND.
- (c) Direct clients from Kijiji or Facebook Marketplace can in principle pay on the day of the job. I did not verify any platform rules or payment norms for these channels, and time to a first Kijiji/Facebook booking was NOT FOUND.

October timing note: I found no source on when move-outs peak in the month (e.g. month-end clustering in Toronto), so that is NOT FOUND.

pricing_facts.fact: Toronto 2026: the typical rate is $35–$65 per hour per cleaner, and most reputable companies charge $45–$55/hr. (From a search-result summary; the result set included this Hellamaid 2026 article, HomeStars, MeshMaids and others. I could not confirm which page the figure came from, and the page fetch was blocked.)

Registered cleaning companies charge $40–$90/hr and include insurance, vetted staff and backup cleaners. Independent cleaners typically charge $15–$30/hr. (Search-result summary for Toronto 2026 cleaning prices; which page it came from is not confirmed.)

Hourly house-cleaning rates in Toronto and Vancouver commonly run $85–$125, versus $65–$90 in mid-sized cities such as Halifax, Winnipeg and Regina. (Search-result summary. It is unclear whether this is per cleaner or per team, and whether it came from the HomeStars 2026 price guide; the page fetch was blocked.)
A standard three-bedroom home in Toronto costs roughly $150–$300 to clean (search-result summary, 2026 Toronto price guides).

Move-out flat rates at 'one major Toronto cleaning service': studio/1BR $325 + HST, 2BR $365, 3BR $443, 4BR $508, 5BR $559 + HST. (Search-result summary; the result set included the Master Maid price list. Attribution is not confirmed.)
A Toronto competitor advertises 'Move Out Cleaning in Toronto | From $185 Fixed' (page title seen in search results).
A standard flat-rate clean for a condo or small apartment is often $165–$250; a larger home or a deep clean is $250–$400+ (2025 Toronto flat-vs-hourly article, search summary).
Apartment cleaning in Toronto typically costs $100–$250, more for deep cleaning and move-in/move-out (search summary).

Rush jobs (within 24 hours, on weekends or on statutory holidays) often carry a 10–20% premium. Downtown Toronto jobs can include paid parking and extra time moving through condo buildings (elevators, key rules). A property with heavy grease, pet hair and odours can be quoted about $180 higher (2026 article, search summary).
TaskRabbit Toronto: house cleaning prices begin at $40, and one-time cleaning starts at $35/hr (search summary of TaskRabbit Canada location pages).
Airbnb/STR turnover per-clean rates in Toronto: NOT FOUND (search refused because the session search limit was reached).
Post-construction cleaning rates (per sq ft or per job) in the GTA: NOT FOUND (search refused because the session search limit was reached).
Calgary, Ottawa and Montreal cleaning rates: NOT FOUND in this session.

cost_facts.fact: TaskRabbit Canada: one-time, non-refundable $25 Tasker registration fee, charged only if registration is processed. Paying it does not guarantee you will become a Tasker. (Search summary of TaskRabbit support page.)

TaskRabbit: clients pay a Taskrabbit Service Fee on top of the Tasker's rate (a percentage of the hourly rate). Apart from the registration fee, all fees are charged to clients, not Taskers. (Search summary; the exact client fee percentage was NOT FOUND.)

Jiffy takes a reported 12–18% commission from the consumer's payment. The commission is reportedly not contractually set, so it can vary. (Search-result summary; the result set included UrbanTasker, SideHusl and Ratehub, and attribution is not confirmed.)
Downtown Toronto jobs can involve paid parking fees (a hidden transport cost).

GST/HST: once taxable revenue exceeds $30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters, you must register and charge GST/HST. Registration is due within 29 days of the effective date. This is an added price or margin cost once crossed. (Search summary of CRA pages.)
Cleaning supplies and equipment (vacuum, chemicals, microfiber, etc.): NOT FOUND (no sourced prices; search limit reached, fetch blocked).
General liability insurance and bonding premiums for a Canadian sole-proprietor cleaner: NOT FOUND (search refused because the session search limit was reached).
Ontario business-name registration fee and WSIB obligations for cleaning sole proprietors or helpers: NOT FOUND in this session.

earnings_evidence.claim: Company-side rates in Toronto are $40–$90/hr for registered companies, versus $15–$30/hr for independent cleaners. A solo newcomer without insurance or reviews would likely be benchmarked against the lower band. (Marketing/industry content from cleaning-company blogs, which have a commercial bias.)
TaskRabbit Toronto one-time cleaning is listed from $35/hr. Because client service fees are charged to the client, the Tasker rate is what the Tasker earns (before their own costs).
Jiffy Pro app reviews (anecdotal) complain that 25–30% of income is taken as commission, which is higher than the 12–18% reported elsewhere.
A 'How much can Canadians make on TaskRabbit?' article exists (FinlyWealth), but I did not see its content or figures, so they are NOT FOUND.
Verified monthly net earnings reports from solo cleaners in Canada (Reddit, YouTube or forums): NOT FOUND in this session (Reddit fetch blocked; search limit reached).

dossier.path_to_5k_math:
All figures below are ESTIMATES built only from the sourced prices above. Direct costs (supplies, transport, insurance) were NOT FOUND, so they are shown as scenarios.

(A) Hourly work. Hours needed = $5,000 ÷ hourly rate; weeks per month = 4.33.
- Zero direct costs:
  - $35/hr (TaskRabbit Toronto starting rate): 5000/35 = 142.9 billable h/month = 33.0 h/week.
  - $45/hr (low end of the reputable-company band): 5000/45 = 111.1 h/month = 25.7 h/week.
  - $55/hr: 5000/55 = 90.9 h/month = 21.0 h/week.
  - $65/hr (top of the per-cleaner range): 5000/65 = 76.9 h/month = 17.8 h/week.
- 20% direct costs (placeholder share, not a sourced figure). Gross needed = 5000/0.8 = $6,250.
  - $35/hr: 6250/35 = 178.6 h/month = 41.2 h/week.
  - $45/hr: 6250/45 = 138.9 h/month = 32.1 h/week.
  - $55/hr: 6250/55 = 113.6 h/month = 26.2 h/week.
- Unpaid travel between jobs is extra and was not quantified.

(B) Jiffy commission. At a $45/hr client price, the pro keeps:
- 12% commission: 45 × 0.88 = $39.60/hr.
- 18% commission: 45 × 0.82 = $36.90/hr.
- 30% (reported in reviews): 45 × 0.70 = $31.50/hr.
- Hours for $5,000 at $36.90/hr: 5000/36.90 = 135.5 h/month = 31.3 h/week.

(C) Move-out flat rates:
- Jobs for $5,000 gross: at $185 (a competitor's 'from' price), 5000/185 = 27.0 jobs/month = 6.2/week; at $325 (1BR at a major firm), 5000/325 = 15.4 jobs/month = 3.6/week.
- With 20% costs: 6250/185 = 33.8 jobs/month; 6250/325 = 19.2 jobs/month.
- Hours per move-out job: NOT FOUND, so I cannot convert jobs into hours.

(D) 60-day average. Month 1 starts from zero clients and zero reviews. If month 1 nets $2,000 (illustrative placeholder, not sourced), month 2 would need 10000 − 2000 = $8,000 net to average $5k. At $45/hr with no costs that is 8000/45 = 177.8 h = 41.1 h/week. That is why the 60-day average is unlikely, even though a $5k run rate by month 2–3 is plausible.

(E) HST trigger. At $6,250 gross per month, cumulative revenue reaches $30,000 after 30000/6250 = 4.8 months. After that the owner must register and charge GST/HST, or absorb it.

(F) Scaling past what one person's labour can earn needs helpers or subcontractors. Employment standards, WSIB and payroll obligations were NOT researched (NOT FOUND).
dossier.startup_cost_cad:
Sourced minimum: $25 (TaskRabbit Tasker registration fee, https://support.taskrabbit.com/hc/en-ca/articles/360032936511-What-s-the-Registration-Fee).

Everything else is NOT FOUND in this session:
- supplies and equipment (vacuum, chemicals, microfiber, mops, caddy)
- general liability insurance or bonding premium
- business-name registration
- any vehicle or transit cost
- phone/data plan

Jiffy pros pay no upfront fee in the sourced material; Jiffy's commission is taken from job payments (12–18% reported). Get real quotes (retail supply prices and an insurance quote) before committing. No capital figure is asserted here, because none was sourced.
requirements: PHYSICAL LABOUR: required and central. $5k net takes roughly 21–41 billable hours a week of standing, bending, scrubbing and carrying equipment, depending on price and costs (ESTIMATE; see the math section). The owner does all the cleaning personally unless they hire.
AGE: 19 or older to be a TaskRabbit Tasker in Canada (https://www.taskrabbit.ca/locations/toronto/house-cleaning, per search summary).

ENGLISH: functional English is needed for platform messaging, quotes, reviews and handling complaints on TaskRabbit/Jiffy. A Korean-speaking client niche (Korean community and realtors) is possible but not researched. The level of English needed was not formally sourced.

VEHICLE: strongly helpful but not strictly required; there is no sourced rule. Downtown jobs involve paid parking (tidyuphandycrew 2026). Carrying a vacuum and chemicals on transit limits jobs per day (judgment, not sourced). Suburban GTA coverage is much easier with a car.
CAPITAL: small. Supply and insurance costs were NOT FOUND. The $25 TaskRabbit fee is sourced.

INSURANCE: not legally mandated per any source found. Companies market insurance and bonding as the reason they charge more than independents, so it is a competitive requirement for property managers, realtors and higher-paying clients. Premiums NOT FOUND.

LICENCE: no cleaning-specific licence was found in this session (NOT FOUND, not verified as unnecessary). If the owner does STR turnover work, the host (not the cleaner) must be registered with the City of Toronto.

ACCOUNTS (human only): TaskRabbit/Jiffy pro accounts with ID and possibly background checks (background-check requirement NOT FOUND/unverified), a bank account for payouts and e-Transfer, and GST/HST registration once over the $30k threshold.
SCHEDULE: availability on evenings and weekends and at month-end for move-outs (demand timing NOT FOUND/unverified).

regulations.fact: Toronto: short-term rentals are allowed only in the operator's principal residence (where they live and use for bills, taxes and government ID). Entire-unit rentals are capped at 180 nights per year; room rentals while the host stays in the home have no annual cap. (Third-party 2026 guides and City of Toronto page, search summary.)

Toronto STR registration fee for 2026: $375 new, $390 annual renewal (third-party guide, search summary; not verified on toronto.ca because the fetch was blocked). Active registrations, with address and ward, are published on Toronto Open Data and refreshed daily. This could serve as a lead list of legal STR hosts who need turnover cleaning.

BC Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act: the principal-residence requirement took effect May 1, 2024. In designated municipalities with more than 10,000 people (plus some adjacent communities), STRs of less than 90 days are limited to the host's principal residence plus at most one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit on the same property. (Search summary of the gov.bc.ca page.)

BC impact, May 2024 to Feb 2025: entire-property STR listings fell 31% in Kelowna, 24% in Victoria and 22% in Vancouver (provincial ministry figures reported by Canada's National Observer, April 24, 2025). That means fewer investor-owned units needing turnover cleaning in Metro Vancouver.

GST/HST: a small supplier has $30,000 or less in worldwide taxable supplies in a calendar quarter and over the last four consecutive quarters. Once over, the business must register (within 29 days of the effective date) and charge GST/HST, including on the sale that crossed the threshold. (CRA pages, search summary.)
Calgary, Ottawa and Montreal/Quebec STR rules, Ontario WSIB coverage for cleaning sole proprietors, and municipal business licensing for cleaners: NOT FOUND in this session.

ai_can_build: A one-page bilingual (English/Korean) website or landing page with an instant quote calculator. Flat rates by bedrooms and bathrooms for standard, deep and move-out cleans, plus add-ons (oven, fridge, balcony, inside cabinets) and a rush surcharge of 10–20%, matching sourced market practice.
A booking request form that creates Google Calendar holds and sends confirmation or quote emails through Gmail drafts, for the owner to approve and send.
A pricing sheet and job-costing spreadsheet: hours, travel time, supplies used and parking, giving effective $/hr per job, plus a running GST/HST $30k threshold tracker by calendar quarter.
Kijiji and Facebook Marketplace ad copy in several variants (move-out, deep clean, recurring weekly/biweekly), plus Korean-language versions for community groups. The owner posts them.

Outreach email templates and lead lists for property managers, realtors (including Korean-speaking realtors in the GTA), condo concierges and small builders (for post-construction work). A lead list of legal Toronto STR hosts from the City's open-data registration dataset. The owner sends the emails.
Printable move-out and move-in checklists, a deep-clean checklist, an STR turnover checklist with photo proof steps, and before/after photo report templates.
TaskRabbit and Jiffy profile copy, service descriptions, and a review-request message sequence.
Invoice and receipt templates (with an HST line ready once registered), a cancellation and lockout policy, and a damage/liability disclaimer draft. A lawyer or insurer should review the disclaimer.
Google Business Profile description and FAQ copy. The owner must create and verify the profile.
human_must_do: All physical cleaning work, travel to jobs, and carrying equipment.
Create and verify accounts that need ID: TaskRabbit ($25 fee), Jiffy Pro, a bank account and e-Transfer, Google Business Profile, and later CRA GST/HST registration.
Buy supplies and equipment, and get and pay for liability insurance and bonding (costs not found; must get quotes).
Post ads on Kijiji, Facebook Marketplace and community groups, and send outreach from the owner's own accounts.
Phone and text conversations with clients, walkthroughs or quotes on site, and handling keys, lockboxes and building access.
Collect payments, handle disputes and complaints, and ask for reviews in person.
Decide on the business name, whether to register it, and whether to hire helpers (which brings in employer obligations not researched here).
dossier.seasonality:
NOT FOUND in the sourced material; no seasonality data was returned in this session. Sourced timing facts only:
- Rush, weekend and statutory-holiday jobs carry a 10–20% premium (https://tidyuphandycrew.ca/2026/02/23/what-affects-move-out-cleaning-cost-in-toronto/).
- Toronto caps entire-home STRs at 180 nights a year, which limits turnovers per listing across the year (https://www.keycafe.com/s/blog/understanding-torontos-short-term-rental-regulations).

Unverified hypotheses to check (NOT facts): move-outs cluster around month-end and the spring/summer moving season; there is extra deep-clean demand before holidays; winter slows STR turnover in Toronto.
risks: Physical injury, strain, or chemical exposure takes the only worker offline, and income drops to zero.

Damage or theft accusations in clients' homes. Without liability insurance and bonding (premiums not found), one claim could wipe out months of profit. Companies use insurance as the reason they charge more (search summary, meshmaids/hellamaid 2026).

Price competition from independents at a reported $15–$30/hr and from TaskRabbit's $35/hr floor. It is easy to underprice and end up with an effective hourly rate below target once travel and supplies are counted.
Platform dependence. Jiffy's commission is reportedly not contractually fixed (12–18% reported, 25–30% in some reviews), payouts are weekly, and ratings and algorithms control who gets jobs.
Unpaid travel time and GTA parking fees reduce the effective hourly rate (parking is sourced; travel time is not quantified).
Toronto and BC STR regulations shrink the market for turnover cleaning: principal-residence-only rules, a 180-night cap in Toronto, and BC listing declines of 22–31%.
Hitting the GST/HST threshold in about month 5 at target revenue (ESTIMATE 4.8 months at $6,250/month). The owner must then charge 'plus HST' or absorb it.
Cancellations, no-shows, lockouts and last-minute reschedules. No sourced frequency data.
Income is capped by one person's hours. Growing past about $5k net requires hiring, which brings employer obligations (not researched).

counter_evidence.fact: Independent cleaners in Toronto reportedly charge only $15–$30/hr, which undercuts newcomers and signals a crowded low end of the market (search summary; page attribution not confirmed).
Established companies differentiate on insurance, vetted and trained staff, and backup cleaners, advantages a solo newcomer lacks at launch (search summary of 2026 Toronto price guides).
Jiffy Pro users complain (anecdotal app-store reviews) of 25–30% commission taken from income. The commission is reportedly not contractually set.
On TaskRabbit, paying the $25 registration fee does not guarantee becoming a Tasker (access risk).
Vancouver entire-home STR listings fell 22% (Kelowna 31%, Victoria 24%) between May 2024 and Feb 2025 after BC's principal-residence rule, reducing turnover-cleaning demand.
Toronto restricts STRs to principal residences, with entire-home rentals capped at 180 nights a year, which limits investor-scale turnover contracts.
Documented failure stories of new cleaning businesses (Reddit or YouTube): NOT FOUND in this session (Reddit fetch blocked; search limit reached).

dossier.score_rationale:
SPEED 7: You can start with almost no setup. TaskRabbit has an active Toronto cleaning category ($25 fee) and Jiffy pays weekly. However, platform approval times were not found, Jiffy's payout lag is 5–11 days (ESTIMATE), and direct clients need reviews and trust first.

PROBABILITY_5K 3.5: The sourced rates ($35–$65/hr per cleaner) mean 26–41 billable hours a week at mid-range prices once costs are counted (ESTIMATE). That target has to be reached from zero reviews, against insured companies and $15–$30/hr independents. Averaging $5k net over the first 60 days would need about $8k net in month 2 if month 1 is a normal ramp-up (illustrative ESTIMATE). A $5k/month run rate by month 2–3 is realistic only for a fit, full-time owner with workable English and ideally a vehicle.

CAPITAL_LIGHT 8: The only sourced upfront cost is $25. Supplies and insurance costs were NOT FOUND, but the business needs no inventory or lease. A vehicle, if not already owned, would change this score a lot.

AI_LEVERAGE 3: The AI can build all the marketing, quoting, booking, checklists and bookkeeping. But roughly 80%+ of the value is physical labour and in-person trust, which only the owner can provide (judgment, not sourced).

LOW_RISK 6: Legal and regulatory risk is low; I found no licence requirement, though that is unverified. The real risks are bodily injury, damage and theft claims (insurance cost unknown), platform dependence, and the income stopping entirely whenever the owner cannot work.

CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: The evidence base is thinner than required. Only 7 searches returned results before the shared search limit ran out, and every page fetch was blocked, so all facts come from search-result summaries. Turnover rates, post-construction rates, insurance and supply costs, earnings reports and failure stories remain NOT FOUND. Before committing, run a follow-up pass that opens the pages to check these numbers.

verification.verdict:
DOWNGRADE: keep this as a fallback or bridge-income option, not the primary plan.

1. Evidence is unverified. None of the 11 decision-critical claims could be re-opened. All pages were blocked and the search budget was used up, so every price, fee and rule remains unverifiable. The core price inputs also contradict each other: $35–$65/hr per cleaner vs $85–$125/hr vs $15–$30/hr, with the unit unresolved.

2. The October start is uncertain. Platform approval times, background-check requirements and first-month job volume for zero-review pros are all NOT FOUND.

3. The math understates the effort. The arithmetic checks out, but it counts only billable hours. Once unpaid travel and schedule gaps are added, reaching $5k net likely means 35–45+ hours a week of physical work. ESTIMATE: 32.1 billable h/wk / 0.75 = 42.8 h/wk.

4. The 60-day average is out of reach. The dossier itself admits month 2 would need about $8k net (ESTIMATE, 41 billable h/wk) to average $5k over 60 days.

5. Speed is still its strength. Upfront cost and legal barriers appear low: no licence was found, though that is not verified as unnecessary.

Overall, it is a plausible way to get some cash quickly for a physically fit, English-capable owner, ideally with a car. It is unlikely to average CAD $5k/month net in the first 60 days, and AI can do only about 20–25% of the work.

Before committing, the owner should personally check:
- TaskRabbit and Jiffy approval times and fees
- a real liability insurance quote
- current prices on 5–10 live Toronto competitor pages
